job.style: a news-style report about a real-world situation

response.passage: On May 12, the bustling town of Bikaner experienced an unprecedented heatwave that pushed mercury levels to a staggering 48 degrees Celsius. Local meteorologist Dr. Arjun Singh reported that the extreme heat was primarily caused by dry, hot winds blowing from the Thar Desert. As the temperature climbed, the municipal corporation issued a strict advisory for residents to stay indoors between 12 PM and 4 PM. Shopkeeper Ramesh Kumar noted that his daily sales of clay water pots surged as people sought traditional cooling methods. While some residents believed that the intense heat was a result of the high number of tourists visiting the nearby Karni Mata Temple, Dr. Singh clarified that the atmospheric pressure shift was the true culprit. By 6 PM, the heat began to subside, providing relief to the weary population. However, the local administration has warned that if these desert winds continue, the town may face water shortages throughout the month. The district collector, Ms. Sunita Rao, has requested that all citizens conserve water to ensure the supply lasts until the monsoon arrives in July.
response.summary: Bikaner faced a severe heatwave on May 12 caused by hot desert winds. Local authorities have advised residents to stay indoors and conserve water to manage the impact of the rising temperatures.
